catalog_quote: Le phonème /p/ se réalise comme une occlusive bilabiale orale sourde [p] en position initiale et en syllabes accentuées, et comme une occlusive bilabiale orale sonore [b] en position intervocalique non accentuée (y inclus après la nasale syllabique). (§2.2.1.1) ... La palatale [c] se trouve en position initiale (accentuée) devant toutes les voyelles : ... La palatale voisée [ɟ] ne se trouve que devant la voyelle [i] en position post-accentuelle : - suffixe de classe nominale (pluriel) [-ɟi]. - suffixe verbal [-ɟi] (p. 29) ... Nous interprétons [c] et [ɟ] comme variantes d'un seul phonème /c/. La réalisation sourde [c] apparaît en position initiale (accentuée) et la réalisation sonore [ɟ] à l'intervocalique (position non accentuée). (p. 30) ... Règle 1 : quand la voyelle orale courte non arrondie d'une syllabe se trouve dans le voisinage d'une syllabe accentuée, elle est facultativement centralisée vers la voyelle centrale de la même hauteur. (p. 34) ... La description a été menée du point de vue de la phonologie segmentale et elle ne comprend pas une étude du système tonal de la langue. (Résumé) ... Le ton joue un rôle sur le plan lexical aussi bien que sur le plan grammatical. ... Nous observons trois registres tonals : le ton haut (H), le ton bas (B) et le ton moyen (M). (§5, p. 35)

new_statements.translation: The palatal [c] occurs in initial (accented) position before all vowels [...] The voiced palatal [ɟ] occurs only before the vowel [i] in post-accentual position [...] We interpret [c] and [ɟ] as variants of a single phoneme /c/. The voiceless realization [c] appears in initial (accented) position and the voiced realization [ɟ] intervocalically (unaccented position). (pp. 29-30) — Post-accentual position. In this position (generally nominal or verbal suffixes) one finds quite a lot of variation across the four dialects. (p. 27)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nateni is a three-tone language (H, M, B). The only prominence the source recognizes is an undefined 'accent' located on the initial syllable of the lexical stem (noun or verb root): stem-initial = accented, proclitic pronouns before it = pre-accentual, class and verbal suffixes after it = post-accentual. Voiceless stops stay voiceless in the accented initial syllable and voice intervocalically in unaccented syllables; short unrounded vowels centralize optionally next to the accented syllable. No explicit stress rule is formulated; this is an implicit positional label, so the reading (stem-initial accent in a tone language) is provisional.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The accent is only invoked as a conditioning environment (intervocalic voicing of /p t c k/ in unaccented position, pp. 9-12, 30; optional centralization of short unrounded vowels next to an accented syllable, p. 34).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/stem level in citation forms and short sentences: the 'accented' syllable is the initial syllable of the lexical stem; a preceding subject pronoun (pà 'ils') is 'pré-accentuelle', class/verbal suffixes are 'post-accentuelle'. The label is applied consistently across the four dialects (data mainly from Nateni proper, Kouba village). The authors never define 'accent' phonetically and explicitly exclude the tone system from the study; tone (H/M/B) is the contrastive prosody (pp. 15, 35-36).
new_statements.identity_note: Nédellec & Bukies 2008 describe Nateni as a whole (four dialects: naténi/Kouba village = nucl1366, tayari = taya1251, kunténi = kunt1238, okoni = okon1238), with most examples from Nateni proper; the accent labels are applied to all four. Prost 1972 (list of works to obtain) is specifically the Tayari dialect (taya1251).

sources.note: Never defines stress/accent; a segmental phonology that uses 'syllabe accentuée' as a positional label: stem-initial syllable = 'position initiale (accentuée)' (pp. 9, 11, 29-30), preverbal pronoun = 'position pré-accentuelle' (pp. 5, 34), suffixes = 'position post-accentuelle' (pp. 27, 29, 34); voiceless stops /p t c k/ voice intervocalically in unaccented position; vowels centralize next to an accented syllable (p. 34). Three lexical tones H/M/B (pp. 15, 35-36); the authors state the study does not treat the tone system.
